subject: Post-demo validation: end-to-end tail budget & streaming concurrency handshake
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@aldermed.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: demo + initial latency questions

Thanks for the demo today — the team found the streaming example helpful. A few quick items we want to lock down before committing to a POC:

- Our current vendor averages p95 end-to-end ~240ms and p99 ~620ms on peak traffic; we need to understand realistic headroom if we move to Redwood hosted.
- Streaming: many of our requests are long-lived server-sent events (avg 6s per request) with 15 concurrent streams during spikes. How does buffering and batching affect tail latency in that pattern?
- Throughput envelope: baseline 120 req/s with short burst up to 600 req/s for ~90s per hour.

I've attached a sample trace export and our internal SLA draft (tailroom-test-plan.xlsx). Can we get a short mutual action plan with timing for an initial tailroom probe and a step that compares hosted vs. our incumbent?

— Sam
Senior Engineering Manager, AlderMed

Attachments: tailroom-test-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB); demo-recording-20261228.mp4 (link)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@aldermed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 18:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + initial latency questions

Thanks Sam — great context and helpful numbers. High level proposal for next steps (2-phase validation):

Phase 1 (engineering workshop, within 1 week):
- Sync on exact request/response shapes and sampling hooks. We’ll provide lightweight instrumentation snippets to capture client-side timings.
- Confirm traffic envelope for the probe (you listed baseline 120 req/s, burst 600 req/s). Please confirm whether bursts are concurrent or sequential within the 90s window.

Phase 2 (tailroom probe + comparative run, 2–3 business days):
- Synthetic tailroom test: replay representative traffic against Redwood hosted with sampling for p50/p95/p99 and streaming tail distribution. We’ll run 10x short bursts and 1 shadow 90s burst to simulate your pattern.
- Comparative check: run the same harness against your incumbent endpoints (if you can provide a temp testing key) to normalize environment differences.

Preliminary acceptance thresholds we’ll target for hosted (adjustable after first workshop):
- p95 end-to-end: <= 250ms for short RPC-style calls
- p99 end-to-end: <= 550ms for short calls
- Streaming (long-lived SSE): 95th percentile chunk latency <= 180ms, tail chunk p99 <= 420ms when concurrency <= 20 streams

Notes and constraints:
- These thresholds are our starting point for the probe; exact numbers will be refined after we see your traces and payload sizes.
- For streaming workloads, batching and prefix-KV cache behavior can change apparent end-to-end tail characteristics — we’ll instrument at both client and server to attribute latency.

Attachments: streaming-config-snippets.txt (small examples), demo-recording-20261228.mp4 (internal link)

Action items:
- Sam: confirm burst concurrency semantics and share a short trace sample with headers enabled.
- AlderMed: provide a temp endpoint or allow us to hit the incumbent for a normalized comparison (security-approved IPs).
- Ben/Jonas: draft test harness and attribution plan — Ben will handle harness; Jonas will define instrumentation events.

I’ll block 60 minutes for the workshop early next week — please propose two 60-min windows that work for your team.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@aldermed.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + initial latency questions

Quick technical notes to set expectations for the probe:

- Harness: I’ll provide a small Go-based harness capable of replaying recorded traces at controlled RPS and concurrency. It will emit client-side timing, server ingress timestamps, and Redwood token-level breakdowns.
- KV cache + batching: for streamed SSE cases we’ll test both with KV caching enabled and disabled. Caching typically reduces compute but can increase variance at tail due to cache warm/cold boundaries — we’ll include warmup runs.
- Metrics: please include span-level context (start/send/first-byte/last-byte) in your traces so we can align timings. If you can add a short unique request tag for each test window that helps correlation.

I’ve attached the harness snippets and a sample config (streaming-config-snippets.txt). If AlderMed can share the incumbent endpoint for a short window we’ll ensure traffic only originates from our test IPs (list to follow).

— Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@aldermed.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + initial latency questions

Thanks — confirming next steps on our side:

- Burst concurrency: bursts are concurrent across our frontend pool; during the 90s window we see up to 600 concurrent short requests and ~15 concurrent long-lived SSEs.
- We are comfortable with your proposed probe schedule: workshop on Tuesday Jan 5 or Jan 6 (we prefer Jan 5, 10:00am PT).
- Acceptance criteria (for the POC evaluation phase we’ll use):
  - Short RPCs: p95 <= 260ms, p99 <= 600ms
  - Long-lived streaming: chunk p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 480ms
- We can provide a temporary read-only endpoint on the incumbent for 2 hours on Jan 7 (security will whitelist Redwood IPs).

Attachments: tailroom-test-plan.xlsx (updated with traffic shapes), sample-trace-20261228.json (sanitized)

PRIYA RAO
Director, Product Engineering — AlderMed
